title: Consumer Credit — G.19 (Aug 2026 data; the first Q3-2026 reading of what revolving credit COSTS)
source: FED: federalreserve.gov/newsevents/2026-october.htm — the Board's own Statistical Release Calendar for October 2026, fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 92,711 bytes). Its 'Statistical Releases' block carries the row '3:00 p.m. | G.19 - Consumer Credit | 7' verbatim, alongside 'FOMC Minutes / Meeting of September 15-16 | 7' at 2:00 p.m. — the same page and the same fetch that already confirms fomc-minutes-2026-10-07, and the same page family the G.17 entry industrial-production-2026-10-16 is confirmed off. Independently reproduced from a second Fed primary that needs no calendar page: federalreserve.gov/releases/g19/current/default.htm states the governing rule verbatim, '*This release is generally issued on the fifth business day of each month' and 'Release Date*: August 7, 2026', and the fifth business day of October 2026 is Wednesday 2026-10-07 (Oct 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 — Columbus Day falls 10-12, after the count). Cross-checked against 34 realized/scheduled G.19 dates harvested from the Board's own monthly calendar pages 2024-01 through 2026-12, every one of which matches the fifth-business-day rule. Promoted estimate -> confirmed 2026-09-08 by this event's OWN dedicated initial-research session, which is the path the no-self-confirm limit leaves open to a proposing sweep (same path fomc-minutes-2026-10-07 and durable-goods-2026-09-25 used); the proposing entry proposals/consumer-credit-2026-10-07.from-retail-sales-2026-09-16.json filed estimate partly because federalreserve.gov/feeds/release_schedule.html 404s — it does, still, and the live calendar above is the page that replaced it
notes: MEASURED AS A NULL, AND KEPT ON THE CALENDAR ANYWAY FOR ONE REASON. Measured 2026-09-08 on SPY hourly bars across 22 G.19 release days over two years, using release dates harvested from the Board's own calendars: the 15:00-16:00 ET release hour's mean absolute move is 0.1378% against 0.1445% on the 472 non-release days, sd 0.2145% against 0.2142% (variance ratio 1.054). The release hour is, if anything, marginally QUIETER than an ordinary final hour. The apparent +0.10% mean drift (Welch t=2.16) collapses to +0.04% once two contaminated sessions are removed — 2025-05-07, an FOMC DECISION day per federalreserve.gov/newsevents/2025-may.htm, and 2025-04-07, an 8.59% full-session range against the sample's 0.88% median. So the drift is two days of somebody else's news, not this release. The one reason to keep it: the August-data edition is a QUARTERLY TERMS-OF-CREDIT edition. The Board's terms-of-credit history (releases/g19/hist/cc_hist_tc_levels.html) is quarterly only, and the current release's monthly columns carry a rate solely in the mid-quarter month (Apr n.a. | May 20.94 | Jun n.a., with Q2 = 20.94), so 2026-10-07 publishes the FIRST Q3-2026 commercial-bank credit-card APR and new-car-loan rates. That is a price-of-credit read, not a volume read, and it has no substitute on this calendar. WHAT THIS RELEASE CANNOT DO, from the Board's own documentation: G.19 Technical Q&A #19 says verbatim that for BNPL 'many of the major BNPL lenders are newly established non-bank lenders, where there is more limited coverage' and 'the G.19 is not currently able to separately track the volume of originations and outstanding balances of such loans.' The proposing ledger asked this print to adjudicate whether a record $43.3B BNPL- and revolving-funded back-to-school total was borrowed; it can answer the revolving half and is structurally blind to the BNPL half. Kept at low impact deliberately: symbols [], 15:00 ET, no house playbook is macro-keyed, and on 2026-10-07 it lands third on a stacked afternoon behind a 13:00 ET 10-year auction and 14:00 ET FOMC minutes. The one prior instance of the G.19 + FOMC-minutes double in sample, 2026-07-08, produced a +0.01% final hour. Proposed by the retail-sales-2026-09-16 D-8 pulse (2026-09-08); canonical file written by this event's own initial research the same day.
